articles_and_episodes.title: Few Leave on Their Own Terms
articles_and_episodes.summary: by Simon O’Connor I’ve said over many years that very few MPs leave Parliament the way they’d hope, and even fewer leave at a time of their own choosing. Arguably none really do, because MPs are always weighing up the circumstances around them and making decisions accordingly. Most Members of Parliament leave because they lose their electorate seat, or their list ranking is too low to bring them back. Some can see the writing on the wall and jump before they’re pushed, and I’d put Jacinda Ardern’s departure in that category. Plenty of others go because of a scandal. Across every political party, over many years, we can all think of those MPs who had to leave for a variety of inappropriate behaviour. The list is too long to enter here. It happens right across the political spectrum, from moral failings to financial impropriety, and more in between! A few examples might suffice. We all remember NZ First and Winston Peters going with Labour and forming government in 2017, and yet, three years later, with only 2.7% of the vote, the entire caucus was out of Parliament. articles_and_episodes.title: Riding Shotgun – ep 71: When Journalism Lost Its Way We All Did
articles_and_episodes.summary: by Rachel Stewart By the time you see this, the result of the election will likely be known. We may be settled and clear about that part of it, or we may even be heading back to the ballot box. Who knows? But here’s what I do know. Despite the outcome, the variables, and the endless talking heads, we are kind of screwed. Because we’re living in a time where democracy is a veneer, and the results are just shuffling the deck chairs on that iceberg-bound ship. Too negative? Well, maybe. But realistic. Having predicted before the election that if the results weren’t crystal clear, we would have cries of “vote rigging” and “voter suppression”, I take no pleasure in being right. Well, maybe a little bit. But what have we become? I think it’s better to be me. See the veneer of democracy for what it is rather than go all in and lose your freaking mind. The left bloc has certainly shown that they’re prone to bouts of hysteria. It’s a symptom of a much deeper malaise. And that is that trust in not only the body politic has broken but, even more than that, we’ve also lost trust in ourselves. What do I mean by this?
